# Exercises

## Background

In August of 2012, news outlets ranging from the [\textcolor{blue}{Washington Post}](http://www.washingtonpost.com/national/on-faith/poll-shows-atheism-on-the-rise-in-the-us/2012/08/13/90020fd6-e57d-11e1-9739-eef99c5fb285_story.html) to the [\textcolor{blue}{Huffington Post}](http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/08/14/atheism-rise-religiosity-decline-in-america_n_1777031.html) ran a story about the rise of atheism in America. The source for the story was a global poll that asked people, “Irrespective of whether you attend a place of worship or not, would you say you are a religious person, not a religious person or a convinced atheist?” This type of question, which asks people to classify themselves in one way or another, is common in polling and generates categorical data. In this lab we take a look at the atheism survey and explore what's at play when making inference about population proportions using categorical data.


The press release for the poll, conducted by WIN-Gallup International, can be accessed
[\textcolor{blue}{here}](https://irtshdf.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/Gallup-International-um-tru-og-truleysi-2012.pdf). Take a moment to review the report then address the following questions.

## Exercise 2: Hypothesis Testing for Proportions

Table 6 provides *statistics*, that is, calculations made from the sample of 51,927 people who were surveyed. What we'd like, though, is insight into the population *parameters*. You answer the question, “What proportion of people in your sample reported being atheists?” with a statistic; this also provides an estimate for the question “What proportion of people on earth would report being atheists?” which is a question about a parameter.

Although formal confidence intervals and hypothesis tests don't show up in the report, suggestions of inference appear at the bottom of page 6: “In general, the error margin for surveys of this kind is +/- 3-5% at 95% confidence”. Let's practice providing more formalized results.

**Suppose that the status quo established by religion scholars was that the proportion of atheists in the United States in 2012 was 3\% of the population.** We'll perform a hypothesis test to determine if this assumption and our observed statistic are consistent.


**a.** Write out the rule-of-thumb conditions required by *theory-based inference* to perform a hypothesis test for the proportion of atheists in the United States in 2012. Are you confident all conditions are met? [Only text is needed for this part, but you can use code to support your answer.]
